title: A property that reports its changes

blocks.text: A subject can **push** the data with each notification, or observers can **pull** what they need from the subject when told something changed. The page's property-change observer does both: listeners get the old and the new value, and may also read the property.
`PropertyChangeListener<T>` (given) has `void onChange(T oldValue, T newValue)`. Write `ObservableProperty<T>`:

items: `setValue(v)` does nothing when `v` **equals** the current value (by `equals`, not by `==`). Otherwise it stores `v` and calls `onChange(old, v)` on every listener. **The new value is stored before any listener runs**, so a listener that pulls with `getValue()` sees it.
**`null` is an ordinary value**: changing to or from `null` notifies, and never throws.

cases.says: setValue() with a different value stores it and calls onChange(old, new) on every listener; a removed listener hears nothing more.
Setting a value equal to the current one (a different String object with the same text) notifies nobody.
Starting at null, changing to a value and back to null each notify once, without a NullPointerException; null to null is no change.
A listener that calls getValue() inside onChange() already reads the new value.

concepts: A subject can push data with each notification or let observers pull it, and a property-change listener gets old and new values only when the value really changes.
